hypothesis: If Thompson's claim holds, in a molecular species-level mammal phylogeny the order Perissodactyla joins Lagomorpha in a clade that excludes Artiodactyla (the other ungulates) and excludes Rodentia, so Perissodactyla's closest relative among these groups is Lagomorpha.
pass_criterion: In at least 95% of the posterior trees (Data_S7 credible tree sets, plus the MCC tree in Data_S4/S5), the Perissodactyla+Lagomorpha MRCA is younger than both the Perissodactyla+Artiodactyla MRCA and the Lagomorpha+Rodentia MRCA. Equivalently, the clade (Perissodactyla, Lagomorpha) excludes all Artiodactyla and all Rodentia. Both conditions must hold, since the claim has two parts.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if, in more than 50% of the posterior trees, either (a) Perissodactyla is monophyletic with Artiodactyla, or nested in a clade with Artiodactyla/Cetartiodactyla, to the exclusion of Lagomorpha, or (b) Lagomorpha is monophyletic with Rodentia to the exclusion of Perissodactyla. It is also refuted if the patristic distance from Perissodactyla to Artiodactyla is smaller than the distance from Perissodactyla to Lagomorpha in the MCC tree.
interpretation: "Perissodactyles" is Perissodactyla (horses, tapirs, rhinoceroses). "Other Ungulates" is mainly Artiodactyla, including Cetacea, which is nested inside it. "Leporidae" (hares and rabbits) is tested through its order Lagomorpha, which is a modern reinterpretation. Leporidae is only one of the two lagomorph families, and the other is Ochotonidae, so the test uses Leporidae tips specifically. "Rodentia" is the rest of the rodents. "More closely related" is read in the modern phylogenetic sense: sister-group relationship or more recent common ancestor, measured on a molecular tree, not as similarity of skull form. Thompson's evidence was the geometric transformation of the skull, so this test is of the inferred relationship, not of the transformation. Modern phylogenomics is expected to place Perissodactyla in Laurasiatheria and Lagomorpha with Rodentia in Euarchontoglires, which would refute the claim.

dataset.name: Inferring the mammal tree: Species-level sets of phylogenies for questions in ecology, evolution, and conservation
dataset.why_it_fits: It holds species-level mammal phylogenies, including credible tree sets in Data_S7 and MCC trees in Data_S4 and Data_S5. Data_S1 holds the master taxonomy, which maps species to order and family (Perissodactyla, Artiodactyla, Lagomorpha/Leporidae, Rodentia). Fields used: the tip labels, the master taxonomy order and family columns, and the Newick trees. From these I compute clade membership and MRCA ages for the three groups.
